title: The ugly duckling.
lines: It was summer.
At the edge of a pond, among the tall reeds, a mummy duck sat on her nest.
She was sitting on five eggs.
One day she heard crack, crack!
The eggs were hatching.
Out came four cute yellow ducklings.
Cheep, cheep, cheep!
But the fifth egg was bigger than the others.
And it stayed closed.
Mummy Duck waited, and waited.
And at last: crack!
Out came a big, grey bird, with a long neck and big feet.
Hmm, said Mummy Duck.
That's a strange duckling.
But I love him anyway.
The next day Mummy Duck took her children swimming.
The grey duckling could swim very well, even better than the others.
But the other animals laughed at him.
Look, said the hen, what an ugly duckling!
Those big feet!
Those grey feathers!
said the turkey.
His brothers and sisters didn't want to play with him.
The ugly duckling was very sad.
One night he ran away.
He walked through the reeds, across the fields, to a big lake.
There he lived all alone.
Then autumn came.
One evening the duckling saw a group of beautiful birds flying over.
They were completely white, with long, graceful necks.
They were flying south, to the warm countries.
How beautiful they are, thought the duckling.
If only I were that beautiful.
Then winter came.
It was cold, and the lake froze.
The duckling was stuck in the ice.
Brrr!
Luckily a farmer came by.
He broke the ice with his clog, and he took the duckling home, in his warm coat.
There he was allowed to sit by the stove until winter was over.
In spring the duckling went back to the lake.
He spread his wings, and he felt that they had grown big and strong.
He flew over the water.
The beautiful white birds were swimming there again.
The duckling bowed his head, because he thought they would laugh at him.
But then he saw himself in the water.
He wasn't an ugly grey duckling anymore.
He was completely white, with a long, graceful neck.
He was a swan!
A beautiful white swan!
Come and swim with us!
called the other swans.
The children on the bank shouted: Look, that new swan is the most beautiful of all!
And the swan was so happy.
At last he had found his family.
